verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly documents scoped API access tokens for building integrations against its operations. Its first-party CLI manages flags, members, projects, environments, teams and other resources. Its MCP server manages flags, AgentControl configs and observability data, so broad programmatic control is evidenced. However, nothing explicitly claims API/UI parity, and the OpenAPI spec probes returned 404, so the breadth of API coverage is unverified. Missing for 10: an explicit API-parity statement or full API reference coverage of UI features (approvals, experiments, guarded rollouts, metrics), a discoverable OpenAPI spec, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: You can scope your API tokens to restrict the set of operations they can perform. For example, you can build an integration that only has read access
set up and manage your feature flags, account members, projects, environments, teams, and other resources directly from the command line.
you enable the server, then use it to manage flags, AgentControl configs, and observability data with natural language.
